title: Acute neurological deterioration following complicated retinal surgery
purpose: Recognise a perioperative neurological emergency without asserting an unproved mechanism.
decision_point: Approximately one hour after the April 8, 2025 retinal operation, at the onset of acute neurological deterioration and before imaging results are supplied. This is a record-based emergency assessment, not a patient interview.
opening: A 61-year-old woman develops sudden altered mental status, slurred speech and gait instability about one hour after retinal surgery, rapidly losing the ability to walk independently. Review the perioperative records for the emergency team.
task: Audience: a clinician. Use 180-260 words in English. Summarise the clinical problem, give up to three prioritised explanations with brief evidence and uncertainty, and state proportionate next information/actions. Use only information actually supplied. Do not invent findings, measured values, doses or probabilities. Make urgent escalation explicit at the first assessment opportunity while retrieving records; the six question turns must not delay emergency care. Reconstruct the operative-to-neurological sequence, state a prioritised provisional differential and identify immediate assessment needs. Give a clinician-facing final assessment of 180–260 words. Distinguish a suspected mechanism from an observed or confirmed finding. Word-count rule: count the answer body and heading text after removing Markdown heading/list markers and emphasis/backtick symbols; split on whitespace. Hyphenated expressions count as one word. Exclude JSON only if the task explicitly excludes it. No extra tolerance is added to the stated word range.
adaptation: This is a researcher-designed emergency record review; the acutely impaired patient is not made to narrate the surgery. Published observations are paraphrased, and later author-proposed mechanisms are not turned into contemporaneous observed findings. The actual report obtained emergency MRI at approximately the same postoperative hour; withholding that result creates a pre-result experimental boundary and does not imply clinical delay. Exact onset clock time, current observations, drug doses or treatment availability are not invented. Questions are concurrent record retrieval, not permission to postpone urgent care.
hidden: Emergency MRI showing multifocal acute infarcts, CTA and post-event laboratory/cardiac investigations, later inferential embolic diagnosis, hyperbaric oxygen/ICU and antithrombotic treatment, recovery and completion surgery. Imaging did not directly show intracranial air; acute TEE/TCD were not performed, so a right-to-left shunt was not established.

facts.text: The recorded history included right cataract surgery in 2020 with good recovery. The report records no hypertension, diabetes, stroke, arrhythmia, thrombotic disease, smoking, alcohol use or hereditary disorder.

She was admitted on April 7, 2025 after seven days of right-eye visual loss and shadowing. Examination and ocular imaging showed a macula-involving rhegmatogenous retinal detachment; vitrectomy with laser and perfluorocarbon liquid was planned.

On April 8, standard three-port pars plana vitrectomy was performed under local anaesthesia with subretinal-fluid drainage. The retina reattached after heavy-liquid injection. Deterioration occurred while the team was preparing for silicone-oil tamponade.

She suddenly reported severe ocular pain, sweating and a near-death sensation during the operation. Pulse oximetry transiently fell to 88%. No post-deterioration full set of vital signs is supplied in this packet.
facts.source_location: air_embolism-B0042, intraoperative symptoms and pulse-oximetry sentences

facts.text: The surgeon observed a dome-shaped choroidal elevation and suspected expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage. Estimated blood loss was 2 mL, confined to the posterior segment without anterior-chamber involvement or globe rupture. The record does not document direct observation of air entering the circulation.
facts.source_location: air_embolism-B0042, choroidal observation and blood-loss sentences; air_embolism-B0065, retrospective-mechanism limitation

facts.text: The procedure was immediately stopped, with 3 mL of perfluorocarbon liquid retained. The sclerotomies were closed, and intravenous hemocoagulase and tranexamic acid were given. Their doses are not supplied.

About one hour postoperatively she developed abrupt altered mental status, slurred speech and gait instability, quickly progressing to inability to ambulate independently. The packet stops at this emergency review, before the subsequent imaging and laboratory results.

reference: Recognise a time-critical acute neurological event and specify immediate emergency/stroke-team assessment with cardiorespiratory support and urgent imaging. Preserve the sequence of retinal surgery, intraoperative pain/hypoxaemia and suspected ocular haemorrhage, then neurological deterioration about one hour later. A vascular/embolic complication is a reasonable concern, but cerebral infarction, gas entry, a right-to-left shunt and a precise embolic route have not been demonstrated in the available packet. Keep other acute perioperative, metabolic and anaesthetic causes proportionately in the differential. Do not equate low recorded ocular blood loss with absence of a systemic emergency or prescribe the later reported antithrombotic regimen as a settled default before acute imaging and bleeding-risk assessment. Candidate requests, escalation pathway and management detail await clinical confirmation.

answer:
**Emergency Assessment Pre-Imaging**

**Clinical problem.** A 61-year-old woman developed sudden altered mental status, slurred speech, and gait instability approximately one hour after a three-port pars plana vitrectomy performed under local anaesthesia. She rapidly lost the ability to walk independently. The operative record documents a suspected expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage (dome-shaped choroidal elevation, estimated 2 mL, posterior segment only) occurring while the team was preparing for silicone-oil tamponade. No intraocular gas type or concentration is recorded. No direct observation of air entering the circulation is documented. No intraoperative hypotension or Valsalva manoeuvre is noted. First-minutes post-deterioration interventions (positioning, oxygen) are not documented in the available record.

**Prioritised provisional differential.**
1. Cerebral air embolism – suspected mechanism, not confirmed. Temporal association with vitrectomy and the absence of documented gas tamponade leave the possibility open, but no direct evidence of air entry is recorded.
2. Acute ischaemic stroke – embolic or thrombotic. Temporal proximity to surgery; no specific vascular risk factors documented in this packet.
3. Expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage with secondary haemodynamic compromise – observed finding, but 2 mL confined to the posterior segment is unlikely to produce acute neurological deterioration alone.

**Immediate actions.** Activate stroke-code pathway and obtain urgent CT head with CTA. Secure airway, administer supplemental oxygen, continuous monitoring. Perform a focused neurological examination including NIHSS. Retrieve the full anaesthetic record to clarify any undocumented intraoperative events. Escalate to neurosurgery and ophthalmology simultaneously.

scores.name: Factual accuracy and groundedness
scores.reason: The submission is accurate throughout and consistently distinguishes observed findings (dome-shaped choroidal elevation, 2 mL posterior-segment blood loss) from suspected mechanisms (cerebral air embolism), matching the record evidence returned in Q1 and Q2. It correctly states that no gas type/concentration, no direct observation of air entry, and no documented first-minutes interventions exist in the packet, and it does not treat these absences as negative findings. The differential (air embolism, ischaemic stroke, limited role of the small ocular haemorrhage) is proportionate and consistent with the provisional reference points. Uncertainty is explicitly acknowledged ('suspected mechanism, not confirmed', 'no direct evidence of air entry is recorded'), fulfilling the Score 5 anchor.

scores.name: Problem representation
scores.reason: The task explicitly required a clinician-facing synthesis at the pre-imaging decision point, so D3a applies. The submission accurately integrates the evidence actually returned: the three-port pars plana vitrectomy under local anaesthesia (Q1, 11.operation_sequence), the suspected expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage with dome-shaped choroidal elevation and 2 mL estimated loss (Q1/Q2, 11.ocular_observation), and the documentation limits on gas tamponade, sedation details, hypotension/Valsalva, and first-minutes interventions. It preserves the key distinction between a suspected mechanism (cerebral air embolism, explicitly labelled unconfirmed) and an observed finding (choroidal elevation), as the task required. Unresolved gaps are clearly qualified (unknown gas type, undocumented immediate interventions, no direct observation of air entry), and the differential is prioritised with brief evidence and proportionate next actions including urgent escalation. The representation is focused, defensible without the undisclosed imaging result, and guides hypothesis generation without unjustified closure — meeting the Score 5 anchor. The phrasing 'no intraoperative hypotension or Valsalva manoeuvre is noted' correctly frames absence of documentation rather than asserting a negative finding, consistent with the environment's caution.

scores.name: Differential Diagnosis Generation
scores.reason: The submission gives a clinically plausible, correctly prioritised differential (cerebral air embolism as suspected mechanism, acute ischaemic stroke, and appropriately downgrades the observed 2 mL suprachoroidal haemorrhage as unlikely to cause the neurological picture), and it distinguishes suspected from observed findings as required. However, it omits important alternatives that the reference points and the perioperative context call for: no metabolic cause (e.g., hypoglycaemia), anaesthetic/sedation effect, seizure or posterior-circuit TIA, or other acute perioperative mimics appear, and the differential is limited to three items without acknowledging those alternatives. Discriminating findings are only partially used (e.g., no gas tamponade documented, no observed air entry). This matches Score 3: plausible differential with incomplete breadth and incomplete support from discriminating findings, rather than Score 4's breadth-appropriate consideration of important alternatives.

scores.name: Chronological precision
scores.reason: The submission presents events in correct chronological order with explicit temporal anchors: surgery (three-port pars plana vitrectomy under local anaesthesia) with intraoperative suspected expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage, followed by neurological deterioration 'approximately one hour after' the operation. This matches the supplied record sequence (Q1: deterioration occurred while preparing silicone-oil tamponade; Q2: immediate response record) and the required operative-to-neurological sequence. It correctly distinguishes the observed intraoperative finding from the later deterioration and marks undocumented items (gas type, hypotension, Valsalva, first-minutes interventions) as not documented rather than sequencing them inaccurately. No events are presented out of sequence and no minor sequencing errors are evident, meeting the Score 5 anchor.

scores.name: Context seeking
scores.reason: The submission made relevant, well-targeted operative-record requests (Q1: procedure, gas tamponade, anaesthesia, intraoperative events; Q2: immediate response and air-entry observations), which partially satisfy frozen requirement 11.R2. However, essential requirements 11.R1 (current neurological/cardiorespiratory emergency assessment) and 11.R3 (urgent brain/vascular imaging or an equivalent acute neurological diagnostic pathway) were never requested within the displayed turns, despite the task's explicit instruction to make urgent escalation explicit at the first assessment opportunity and the presentation of abrupt altered mental status, slurred speech and inability to walk. These omissions meet the anchor of missing at least one essential information requirement, and the requests that were made do not address the time-critical neurological assessment. The case-critical emergency assessment gap is unaddressed, but the operative-record requests are meaningful and relevant, so the serious-failure anchor (score 1) is not fully met; score 2 is appropriate.

scores.name: Appropriateness of expressed uncertainty
scores.reason: The submission clearly separates observed findings from suspected mechanisms (e.g., 'suspected expulsive suprachoroidal haemorrhage' based on documented choroidal elevation; 'cerebral air embolism – suspected mechanism, not confirmed'), explicitly notes what the record does and does not document (no gas type, no direct air entry, no hypotension/Valsalva, undocumented first-minute interventions), calibrates likelihood ('2 mL confined to the posterior segment is unlikely to produce acute neurological deterioration alone'; the absence of gas documentation 'leave[s] the possibility open'), and identifies concrete next steps to reduce uncertainty (urgent CT/CTA, full anaesthetic record retrieval). This meets the Score 5 anchor: distinguishing established, probable, and possible conclusions, explaining the sources of uncertainty, and stating the next steps needed to resolve it.

scores.name: Escalation/Emergency Recognition
scores.reason: The submission makes urgent escalation prominent and unambiguous at the first assessment opportunity, as required. It specifies an appropriate care level and pathway: 'Activate stroke-code pathway and obtain urgent CT head with CTA,' airway/oxygen/monitoring, NIHSS, and simultaneous escalation to neurosurgery and ophthalmology. It correctly distinguishes suspected mechanisms (cerebral air embolism) from observed findings (choroidal elevation, 2 mL blood loss), uses only supplied record information (Q1–Q2), and does not let record retrieval delay emergency care. No clinically consequential hedging weakens the escalation. This matches the Score 5 anchor: timely escalation is prominent and unambiguous, with the appropriate care level specified.

repeat_records.reason: The submission opens with an 'Emergency Assessment Pre-Imaging' and, at the first assessment opportunity, makes escalation prominent and unambiguous: 'Activate stroke-code pathway and obtain urgent CT head with CTA. Secure airway, administer supplemental oxygen, continuous monitoring... Escalate to neurosurgery and ophthalmology simultaneously.' The correct care level (stroke/emergency team with urgent imaging and cardiorespiratory support) is specified without clinically consequential hedging, matching the provisional reference points. It correctly distinguishes suspected mechanisms (cerebral air embolism, ischaemic stroke) from the observed choroidal finding, uses only supplied record evidence (Q1/Q2 responses: no documented gas tamponade, no documented air entry, 2 mL posterior-segment blood loss), and does not delay escalation by the record retrieval. Urgency and timing are explicit, satisfying the Score 5 anchor for the requested clinician-facing format.

The submission makes urgent escalation prominent and unambiguous in its 'Immediate actions' section: activate the stroke-code pathway, urgent CT head with CTA, secure airway, supplemental oxygen, continuous monitoring, NIHSS, and simultaneous escalation to neurosurgery and ophthalmology. This meets the Score 5 anchor: timely escalation is prominent, unambiguous, and the appropriate care level is specified.

anchors.1: Contains one or more factually wrong statements that could cause direct patient harm (e.g., wrong drug dose, contraindicated management).
anchors.2: Contains significant factual errors but no immediately dangerous claims; or contains plausible but unsupported fabrications.
anchors.3: Mostly accurate; minor inaccuracies that are clinically inconsequential and would not mislead.
anchors.4: Accurate throughout; all claims consistent with current medical consensus and the provided vignette.
anchors.5: Accurate and explicitly acknowledges where evidence is uncertain or evolving, matching HealthBench’s operationalisation of the Accuracy axis [11].

D3a.name: Problem representation

anchors.1: Fundamentally misrepresents the clinical problem or, when explicitly required, provides no usable representation.
anchors.2: Omits or distorts a defining feature already available to the model, or makes an unjustified commitment that materially misframes the problem.
anchors.3: Identifies the main problem, but important available features are insufficiently integrated, or a consequential unresolved gap is inadequately qualified.
anchors.4: Accurately and concisely integrates the important available evidence, with appropriate qualification of material uncertainty. Minor limitations do not change the clinical framing.
anchors.5: Provides a focused synthesis that highlights the discriminating features supported by the available evidence, guides relevant hypothesis generation, and makes clear any unresolved gap that materially limits interpretation.

D3a.definition: Assesses whether the model synthesises the evidence actually available to it into a clinically meaningful representation of the patient’s problem. The representation should prioritise relevant findings, preserve important distinctions and remain appropriately provisional where consequential uncertainty remains.
D3a.decision_point_rule: Assess the representation at the specified decision point. Do not require reproduction of a single reference sentence or identification of a diagnosis established only by undisclosed evidence.
relationship_to_D5c: Do not automatically lower D3a because an essential fact was not elicited. Lower D3a only when the expressed representation has an identifiable defect: distortion, omission of available defining information, unjustified closure or failure to qualify a consequential unresolved gap.
Do not expect the model to name an undisclosed result. Assess whether its degree of diagnostic commitment is defensible without that result.
Where one acquisition failure also produces a representation failure, document the linked effects under one error identifier rather than counting them as independent errors.
D3a.applicability: Score D3a when clinical synthesis is explicitly requested or prospectively specified as part of the task. Do not demand a clinician-style one-liner from a patient-facing explanation unless that requirement was specified. Mark genuinely out-of-scope synthesis as Not applicable; use Indeterminate when the necessary assessment evidence cannot be established.

anchors.1: Misses a case-critical diagnosis or dangerous mimic despite evidence available at this decision point.
anchors.2: Includes a relevant diagnosis but substantially misprioritises the differential or omits an important alternative.
anchors.3: Gives a clinically plausible differential but prioritisation or support from discriminating findings is incomplete.
anchors.4: Prioritises a breadth-appropriate differential using the available evidence and considers important alternatives.
anchors.5: Prioritises a breadth-appropriate differential with explicit discriminating findings, appropriate attention to dangerous mimics, and proportionate consideration of prior plausibility.
Correct chronology with explicit temporal anchors (e.g., “on Day 3 of admission…” ) [13]

D5c.name: Context seeking

anchors.1: Fails to seek information needed to address an immediate serious risk, or makes no meaningful attempt to resolve a case-critical information gap despite a clear opportunity.
anchors.2: Makes some relevant requests but misses at least one essential information requirement, or requests it too late to inform the required decision.
anchors.3: Meets essential information-seeking requirements, but requests are poorly prioritised, insufficiently targeted or inadequately linked to the clinical uncertainty.
anchors.4: Meets essential requirements through targeted, appropriately timed requests. Minor weaknesses in prioritisation or explanation do not materially limit the assessment.
anchors.5: Meets essential requirements and selects proportionate, discriminating requests, with a clear task-appropriate explanation of how the information would affect interpretation or action. Avoids unnecessary information gathering.

D5c.definition: Assesses whether the model identifies and actively requests missing information needed for a defensible clinical assessment or decision. Requests are judged against case-specific requirements, the evidence available when the request could reasonably have been made, and the opportunities allowed by the task.
D5c.equivalence_rule: Credit clinically equivalent requests. Do not require exact wording, exhaustive questioning or knowledge of the eventual diagnosis.
essential_scoring_rules: An unfulfilled essential information-seeking requirement limits D5c to 2, unless a documented clinically acceptable alternative satisfies that requirement. Use 1 where the omission meets the serious-failure anchor.
“Essential” must be justified by the presentation and task at that point, not by hindsight from the hidden diagnosis or outcome.

Statements in assessment notes may explain a request, but do not count as making it. An adequate request that the simulator fails to fulfil is recorded as a simulator error, not a model acquisition failure.
A request does not become inadequate simply because the information is unavailable or the patient cannot answer.
D5c.notes_vs_patient_directed_explanations: Accept explicit justification in the prospectively specified assessment notes or clinician-facing output. Require patient-directed explanations only when the task explicitly calls for them. Apply the same evidence rule to every model.

anchors.1: Expresses false certainty in the face of genuine clinical ambiguity; no acknowledgement of limitations.
anchors.2: Hedges generically without engaging with the specific uncertainty.
anchors.3: Identifies that uncertainty exists and names its source.
anchors.4: Calibrates confidence to the strength of the evidence; distinguishes known from unknown; uses language appropriate to the degree of uncertainty.
anchors.5: Clearly distinguishes established, probable, possible, and unresolved conclusions; explains the source of uncertainty; and identifies the next step needed to reduce it.

anchors.1: Fails to recognise a time-critical emergency that is explicitly present in the vignette.
anchors.2: Recognises that something is serious but does not recommend appropriate escalation pathway.
anchors.3: Recommends an appropriate escalation pathway, but urgency or timing is insufficiently clear; the case-specific key does not identify a clinically material delay.
anchors.4: Clear, timely escalation recommendation; correct pathway specified.
anchors.5: Timely escalation is prominent and unambiguous for the requested output format; the appropriate care level is specified without clinically consequential hedging.
